samples.summary: Adding `readOnly` to the editor effect's deps makes editor/store re-creation reachable, but `YorkieDocStore` never unsubscribes from the Yorkie doc — the old store keeps firing `onRemoteChange` against a disposed editor
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore`'s constructor (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:622) calls `doc.subscribe(...)` and DISCARDS the returned unsubscribe handle; the class has no `dispose()` (grep for `unsub|dispose|detach` in that file returns only an unrelated comment). The effect cleanup (docs-view.tsx:549-571) disposes the editor and nulls `storeRef`, but never clears `store.onRemoteChange` and cannot unsubscribe the old store. Before this delta the effect only re-ran on `[didMount, doc]` (a new doc = a new subscription target anyway); with `readOnly` in the deps, a permission flip on the SAME doc (exactly the 'share link re-resolving from editor to viewer' scenario the new comment cites, and also the common 'permission resolves after first paint' flip) leaves the previous store subscribed. On every subsequent remote change that stale closure runs `editor.clearImageSelection(); editor.getDoc().refresh(); editor.restoreLocalCursor(...); store.publishResolvedLocalCursor(...); editor.render()` on an editor whose canvas was already removed by `dispose()` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4412) and whose measurer cache was released — wasted full-document parses, a presence write of the DEAD editor's cursor that races the live store's cursor presence (peers see the caret jump), and one leaked store+editor per toggle.

samples.summary: Restoring `dirtyBlockIds` makes the post-undo-unit repaint incremental against a layout cache measured from writes that a throw may have rolled back
samples.evidence: `requestLayoutRefresh` now leaves `dirtyBlockIds` set (or an empty Set) so the deferred paint reuses `layoutCache`. But that cache was built by the mid-batch pass from the IN-PROGRESS document (`YorkieDocStore.readRoot()` reads `activeRoot` during the open `doc.update`). `withUndoUnit` (text-editor.ts:3840-3850) replays the held `requestRender()` in its `finally`, i.e. also after a throw, and its doc comment promises 'the screen always shows what the store really holds'. On `YorkieDocStore` a throw rolls the whole batch back, yet the replayed render now consults per-block cached `lines` measured from the rolled-back state, and for the `dirty === undefined` branch it consults them with an EMPTY dirty set, so nothing is re-measured. Previously the second pass was unconditionally full (`dirtyBlockIds === undefined` → `canUseCache` false in layout.ts:456), which masked this. Result: the canvas can paint text the store does not contain until the next full invalidation.

samples.summary: The restored (possibly empty) dirty set removes the full-recompute safety net that hid any in-unit write missing a `markDirty`/`invalidateLayout`
samples.evidence: Before this change, the paint that follows an undo unit always ran with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined` and therefore re-measured every block, so any write path inside a unit that forgot to mark its block dirty still rendered correctly. With `dirtyBlockIds = dirty ?? new Set()` the post-unit paint is incremental and reuses `cache.blocks.get(id).lines` (layout.ts:535) for every unmarked block, so a single missing `markDirty` now shows stale text on screen. The correctness of every batched edit path (e.g. `insertPlainText` at text-editor.ts:4287-4314, `insertBlocks`, `pasteTableCells`, `applyHangulResult`) now depends on exhaustive dirty-marking that nothing enforces or tests.
searchedFor: read deleteSelectionImpl, insertPlainText, insertBlocks, handleEnter, applyHangulResult
read computeLayout cache branch in packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts

samples.summary: The Hangul commit-over-selection unit (newly pinned by this delta's test) opens `withUndoUnit` without the required preceding `saveSnapshot()`
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit`'s contract (text-editor.ts:3828-3838) is '`saveSnapshot()` must be called before opening a unit, never inside one', because on `YorkieDocStore` it is what flushes the PRE-edit caret/selection into presence for undo to restore. The jamo branch of `handleInput` (line 1005-1009) returns before the `saveSnapshot()` at line 1014, and `applyHangulResult`'s commit-with-selection branch goes straight to `this.withUndoUnit(() => { this.deleteSelection(); this.docInsertText(...) })` with no snapshot (the preview branch at 5911-5915 does call it). The new test 'a Hangul commit over a select-all is one undo unit' asserts only text restoration, which `MemDocStore.batch()`'s own checkpoint satisfies, so the missing pre-edit caret/selection on the Yorkie path is unobserved: undoing that commit restores the post-edit caret instead of the select-all range.

samples.summary: The added `this.readOnly` re-check in `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` cannot fire — `readOnly` is immutable for the life of a `TextEditor`
samples.evidence: `this.readOnly` is assigned exactly once, in the constructor (line 719); there is no setter (grep `this.readOnly` shows only reads elsewhere). So it holds the same value at the clipboard-resume point as it did at the keydown gate, and the comment's rationale ('the permission this session is allowed to exercise is the one that decides — not the one that held when the shortcut was pressed') does not describe what the code does. A permission change is handled by rebuilding the whole editor (docs-view.tsx:581), which sets `disposed` — already covered by the existing check on the same line. Harmless, but the comment asserts a guarantee the guard does not provide.

verdict.reason: The described code is present exactly as claimed: YorkieDocStore's constructor subscribes to the Yorkie doc and throws away the unsubscribe handle (yorkie-doc-store.ts:622-627), and the class exposes no dispose/teardown (only match for subscribe/dispose/unsub/detach in the file is that constructor plus an unrelated comment at :2918). The editor effect's cleanup (docs-view.tsx:549-571) unsubscribes only presence, disposes the editor and nulls storeRef, but never clears store.onRemoteChange (installed at :410-439) nor unsubscribes the store, so a re-run leaves the old store live and firing clearImageSelection/refresh/restoreLocalCursor/publishResolvedLocalCursor/render against an editor whose canvas was removed and whose measure cache was released (editor.ts:4382-4413) — wasted parses plus a presence write of the dead editor's cursor racing the live store. Adding readOnly to the deps at :581 makes re-run reachable without a doc change (readOnly is derived from resolved.role in shared-document.tsx:322/364), and the same stale-store defect is independently reachable today via docs-detail.tsx:350 mounting DocumentProvider above <DocsView key={historyResetToken}> at :280-281, where a history restore remounts DocsView while the same doc stays attached. No guard anywhere clears or unsubscribes the previous store.
